Juliana Stratton

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, Illinois · Open seat

Lieutenant Governor of Illinois

Juliana Stratton is the Democratic nominee for the open U.S. Senate seat in Illinois. Incumbent Democrat Dick Durbin is retiring. She has been Illinois' lieutenant governor under Gov. JB Pritzker since 2019, and she won the Democratic nomination in the 2026 primary.

Where Stratton stands

Tariffs and trade
Opposes President Trump's tariffs and calls for ending them. She says they caused a trade war with U.S. allies and raised prices, and calls the trade policy illegal.
Oversight of the president
Says she will "be a check on this president" and hold President Trump accountable if elected.
Presidential nominees
Pledged not to vote to confirm any of President Trump's nominees.
War in Iran
Says she will not vote for any bill that provides supplemental funding for the war in Iran. She blames President Trump for starting the war.
Cost of living
Says President Trump's tariffs and the war in Iran have pushed up the cost of living, including gas prices.

Background

  • Lieutenant Governor of Illinois (48th), 2019–present
  • Illinois State Representative, 5th District, 2017–2018 (per Daily Herald questionnaire)
  • Kenwood Academy Local School Council member, 2012–2015
  • 2026 Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Illinois
  • Lives in Chicago; age 61 (per Daily Herald, October 2026)
